newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh police arrest wife of fugitive colonel.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh police arrest wife of fugitive colonel.

text.p: Bangladesh police have arrested the wife of a fugitive army colonel who is wanted for his alleged role in the killing of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the country's independence leader, newspapers reported on Monday.
Colonel Abdur Rashid is facing charges of masterminding Bangladesh's first military coup on August 15, 1975, in which Mujib was killed along with most of his family.
Newspaper said police arrested Zobaida Rashid at her residence in Dhaka on Saturday night on charges of possessing unauthorised firearms.
She was sent to court on Sunday and later placed in police remand for five days for interrogation, the reports said.
Police refused to comment, but said they had seized movable property from Rashid's house last week. They gave no details.
The colonel left the country after Mujib's daughter Sheikh Hasina, who took over as prime minister after general elections in June, announced plans to hunt down her father's killers.
Rashid's wife told reporters last week that her husband was in Libya. But her daughter Mehnaz Rashid said on Sunday that he had spoken to her from London.
Hasina and her only sister Sheikh Rehana survived the 1975 coup as they were travelling abroad at the time.

Police have already arrested about a dozen suspects, including two of Rashid's close comrades -- colonel Farook Reehman and Shahriar Rasheed Khan -- as part of a recently launched inquest into Mujib's killing.

Police have said that they were seeking Interpol's help to find and bring home six former army officers, suspected masterminds of the coup but later assigned to diplomatic jobs by Mujib's successors. All six, including Rashid, have absconded since the June general elections.
